answer: Zero-knowledge proof of a unique credential stops sybils: each identity must prove it holds a distinct credential, such as a passport, without revealing it, and publish a one-time nullifier for that epoch. Like an onyx seal that stamps only one impression, the same credential cannot mint a second identity, and each vertex in the trust graph may occupy only one place on the knoll of members. An honest user proves once, cheaply and privately, while an attacker wanting a thousand voices must acquire a thousand credentials, each costly and risky to obtain, and each spent after a single use.
